bypass_paths.evidence: Only the $default stage and no mapping path, verified by the configuration check, and the stage check of the event; case AWS-10

unsupported_forms: Direct PACT enforcement across arbitrary AWS services (sample I09): only the routes of one custom API are claimed
Inherited caller authority for the execution role (sample I09): the execution role is a distinct actor with its own declared permissions
REST APIs, WebSocket APIs, payload format 1.0, non-proxy and HTTP integrations: payload 1.0 has no rawQueryString and the REST proxy event does not preserve the order of request parameters
JWT and Lambda authorizers, IAM users, the root user, federated users, and Amazon Cognito credentials: only assumed-role sessions map to a workload
Callers from another account than the API owner's

Shared roles, and telling agents apart by session name or source identity: one role per agent, the default of identity-mapping section 5; a role with more than one enrollment in force is a configuration error (AR-12), and session names are chosen by the caller
Telling sessions of one role apart by session policy: the event reports no session policy, so the identifier uses unreported
Named stages, API mappings with a path, more than one domain, and the default endpoint: the path in the event would not be the path the client sent
The $default route, greedy path variables, and the ANY method: a mapping row could not predict the requests it receives
Routes that accept a body: body octets are not established for text bodies (probe P8)
Query-string Signature Version 4 authentication: credentials would enter target_uri
Presentations that exceed the 10240-byte request line and header budget of an HTTP API: no envelope or validator transfer is defined (open item O7)

Any field of the I09 profile other than principal_id, workload_role, and account_id, such as the delegation authority_ref and the runtime isolation evidence: supplied by the deployment outside this profile
Any route other than the reference route of protected_routes: not listed, so not claimed
Agents' direct calls to AWS services, and calls by other principals: excluded by their out_of_claim control in bypass_paths

residual_limits: Post-read: metrics already returned to the agent are not recalled by a later revocation of a session or an enrollment, and no egress or data-use control is claimed; disclosed here with no bound

Revocation propagation, role session: temporary credentials stay usable until they expire, at most 43200 s after issue, unless the role's sessions are revoked; IAM is eventually consistent and no page read states a bound for API Gateway's authorization, so the deployment declares L (illustrative 60 s)
Revocation propagation, enrollment: a revocation or compromise mark reaches the gateway within the 0 second status bound of the registry, inside the consistency of the registry backend

Revocation propagation, role table and configuration: a removed role entry takes effect at the next event after reload; an AWS configuration change that breaks the supported form is seen at the next configuration check, within P (illustrative 300 s)
Session policy: sessions of one role under different session policies are one workload; a session policy can only narrow the role
Direct invocation: the event carries no proof of its invoker; the claim rests on the resource-policy deny that probe P4 must show effective, and is a precondition of the enforced claim
Raw target: request binding relies on rawPath and rawQueryString carrying the request-target unchanged, which probe P2 must show; a precondition of the enforced claim
Header field lines: several field lines of a covered header and one line with commas bind alike
Header budget: a presentation larger than the 10240-byte request line and header budget cannot be presented, and no evidence is truncated or dropped

Execution role scope: the execution role can do whatever its own policy allows; the profile verifies neither that policy nor its trust policy, and the deployment declares the permissions of each translation row (open item O4)
Session name: a session-name rule can refuse sessions but never proves which process created a session
